# Temporary braces 3.0.3 security backport

This is the original MIT-licensed `braces` 3.0.3 package with five library-file changes from [upstream pull request 72](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/pull/72), pinned at `28d440b5dd449dbf1fe6f3506cf94ecca4d02660`. It retains its original package name and version. Its package metadata marks this local copy private, omits upstream development-only tools, and points its test command to the included security regression. It is not an official new upstream release.

As checked on 2026-10-03, [GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm / CVE-2026-93687](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) has **no published patched version**. The advisory affects recursive processing of deeply nested brace patterns. The current Next ESLint plugin and Vinext glob tooling still reach this dependency; automatically downgrading either toolchain is not a compatible remedy.

The backport limits parsed brace/parenthesis nesting and directly supplied AST depth to 100, honors stricter limits, and rejects cyclic AST parent chains during expansion. It includes the upstream follow-up preserving `escapeInvalid` behavior. `SECURITY.patch` is the exact five-file backport; `source-manifest.json` records the original published-file and resulting SHA-256 hashes. All other JavaScript files are unchanged from 3.0.3. The original license remains in `LICENSE`.

The original installed release was independently observed to throw `Maximum call stack size exceeded` for 4,998 nested brace pairs around `a,b` (9,999 characters) in `expand` and `stringify` on Node 24.21.0/Windows. The backport rejects this same input at nesting level 101, before recursive processing.

The root development dependency installs this directory and the `$braces` override reference uses that same resolved package for every transitive dependency. The direct file dependency is required for a portable npm lockfile: a bare transitive `file:vendor/braces` override can resolve relative to a consumer. npm does not obtain registry advisories for a local file package, so a zero audit count **alone is not evidence of remediation**. The independently executed regression suite checks the advisory's deeply nested input, direct ASTs, parent cycles, 100/101 boundaries, fractional limits, escaped/malformed compatibility and the actual installed micromatch/fast-glob paths. These tests run with the regular unit suite. No audit ignore, severity reduction, fake package rename or toolchain downgrade is used.

Remove the local override and this directory when upstream publishes a fixed compatible release; retain the regression checks when upgrading. The patch addresses the documented nesting/cycle vulnerability, not every possible resource cost of arbitrary glob expansion. This is development tooling, not an application circuit parser or browser dependency.
